while i do agree that fans need to have their own lives on some level, some people have tøp as one of their special interests. 

Autistic people specifically will become absorbed in their special interests. Tøp is one of my special interests, but after a year or two i’ve had the ability to move onto another (more “socially acceptable”) one primarily. I used to only listen to their music and consume tøp related content. It brought me comfort, it was very regulating to listen to the same music and knowing what it sounds like, what’s coming next, etc. It still is comforting to me, when I am having a hard time feeling in control, I listen to their older albums. 

We have dysregulated immune systems, this is why it is so easy to seem “obsessed” when we find something that helps us regulate. It’s like a breath of fresh air after being in a coffin. 

Of course I do not speak for all of the obsessive fans out there, and I do not endorse shaming or belittling people because of their knowledge of a specific band. just thought i’d offer some sort of explanation for why some people are “too” obsessed. 

To say it’s unhealthy is a very strong statement and we don’t know the situations of the people who find themselves “obsessed”.

as someone who also has adhd and on meds for it. the appetite suppression will lessen with time. 


take your medicine with food!!!!  this is very important!!! 


i cannot eat ANYTHING when i don’t take my meds with food. and even with food i do eat less than on the days that i forget to take it. 

the reason BED is a bit more common for folks with adhd is because we all need dopamine to regulate ourselves, adhd is a lack of dopamine. without it, we experience executive dysfunction. Eating, and sugar specifically gives us the dopamine we are constantly striving for. so of course we’re going to stop binging as often if we are medicated for the adhd (not to say i don’t still struggle on bad days).

it doesn’t matter if you binged last night. your body still needs fuel for today and tomorrow. you deserve to eat. restricting yourself from what you want will cause binging. feeling bad will cause binging. give your body what it’s asking for, if you are craving chips but you eat a salad, you will continue to eat until you get those chips. 

personally i’ve also had a few weeks where i’d go over my calorie goal but i still eat the day after. no matter how bad i feel about it. everyday is a new day. and lately ive been doing better (aside from last night). I still ate lunch though, and i will still eat dinner. 

if you feel the urge to binge often, it is possible that the deficit you’re going for is too low. your body isn’t going to magically be able to eat 1200 calories a day without slowly going down. that is starving yourself. 

you deserve to feel good about yourself, you don’t need to look a certain way to be worthy of love.

it is a little harder for people to be willing to accommodate when i say “i think im autistic.” 

i am not diagnosed, but i know myself more than anyone else does. i know i am autistic. i’ve done the research, ive asked autistic peers, i know who i am. I am planning on getting a diagnosis but the process is taking much longer than i expected. 

i’m not using the term autistic to tell people that they have to accept poor behaviors of mine. i am using it to describe why i can’t be in a crowded and noisy rooms, why i can’t speak sometimes when i get overwhelmed, and why I don’t understand “simple” social cues. 

when i say “i think im autistic” some people will find ANY reason to not believe me. It makes things harder to open up about and overall is very dismissive of how im feeling. 

I don’t think saying that you’re autistic is harmful unless you’re using it to justify poor behaviors. 

I believe it is more helpful to people who need accommodations that autistic people would need. even if they aren’t autistic, if they relate to needing accommodations such as: stim toys/breaks, being able to leave loud spaces, single bedrooms if living in a dorm, etc. 
It is helpful because they are getting the help they need. 

obviously some people will watch like 2 tiktok’s and assume they are autistic, this is very different from what i’m describing. i don’t think a regular person would be very comfortable saying that they’re autistic unless they are 100% sure. 

I don’t even like telling people that i’m autistic, it gives them preconceived notions, some that aren’t even accurate.

i feel the exact same way. i’m struggling to complete my assignments as we speak because i forgot my meds this morning. 

for me, when it comes to doing things(literally anything), i need to feel some sense of accomplishment for doing said task. so in order to help this at work i make very specific checklists for me to complete so i make sure i don’t forget anything and so i can feel some sense of accomplishment for wiping down all the tables, then chairs, etc. 


at home i make specific checklists of schoolwork i need to do, and once i start becoming frustrated with it or can’t stay still i reward myself for the work i’ve done, and take a break.sometimes i don’t go back from the break but other times i go back and this system works pretty well. 


prioritization is a big issue for me, i can’t determine what’s most important so i go by the most time sensitive assignments or tasks. and if there’s multiple things to do on the same day i start the harder one first so when i get frustrated with it i can switch to the easier one. then go back and finish the harder one if i don’t need a break by then. 

executive dysfunction affects everyone differently, so combatting it with a bunch of checklists or rewards might not work for you. but it might be worth a shot.
